display.title: Episode 537: The Ten Wedding Gifts, Chapter 4 (Yud-Gimmel Tammuz)
display.summary_short: No vacation from Torah, the final chapter of the Ten Wedding Gifts, and a Yud-Gimmel Tammuz talk on Hashem hidden in nature and the Frierdiker Rebbe's miraculous release.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Yud-Gimmel Tammuz 5752. Uncle Yossi opens with a vacation message: Torah and mitzvos are the 'breath of life', and just as we never stop breathing, there is no vacation from learning and davening, whatever the yetzer hara says. After the Hakochainik march, a girl from Beis Rivkah leads the Shema and tells listeners how much fun it is to belong to Tzivos Hashem, and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time brings the final chapter of 'The Ten Wedding Gifts': Avraham and Sarah bring the lost boy home, and his grateful father, the poritz, makes a royal banquet in their honor. He gives them the town park, another poritz gives the lumberyard, and one by one all ten gifts promised by the Baal Shem Tov's students come true. Next Uncle Yossi explains that 'Elokim' and 'HaTeva' (nature) share the same gematria, 86: Hashem hides inside nature, and sometimes lifts the veil with open miracles. Yud-Beis and Yud-Gimmel Tammuz celebrate such a miracle, the release of the Frierdiker Rebbe, who had been sentenced to death for teaching Torah to children. The show ends with Tehillim for the Rebbe's recovery and candle-lighting time.
display.lesson: Hashem rewards kindness in full measure, even if it takes time; He is hidden in nature but always in charge. And there is no vacation from Torah and mitzvos.

date.note: 'Today is Yud-Gimmel Tammuz', which fell on Tuesday 14 July 1992; Friday candle-lighting 8:06 matches; prayers for the Rebbe's recovery confirm 5752.

advisories.note: The Frierdiker Rebbe was imprisoned and sentenced to death for teaching Torah; he was saved.
